problem_type: Product-name heuristics lack the exact legacy alias relationship used by runtime identity
symptom: check:platform-archetypes counts gpt-image-2 as four products after Codex Img2 aliases are preserved.
direct_cause: String-stem clustering treats gpt-4o-image, codex-img2 and codex-imagegen-img2 as unrelated products.
class_root: Curated exact same-product aliases need one shared canonical identity before either runtime matching or product classification.
affected_population: Existing GPT Image 2 and Codex Img2 model keys/aliases
internal_only_reason: This records existing repository alias semantics, not a claim that different provider models have identical external capabilities; no external product identity is inferred.
invariants: Only exact declared aliases canonicalize; unknown versions remain distinct.
Catalog and renderer use the same alias owner as the platform gate.
Existing identifierPatterns, generated identity table, Codex Img2 catalog labels and baseline remain unchanged.
Unrelated products within any profile, including gpt-image-2, still fail the original threshold.

door_reduction.why_not: The union of the generated public-resolver consumer map and generated canonicalArchetypeIdentifier/PRODUCT_IDENTIFIER_ALIASES map adds four shared-boundary edges. Catalog listing, health, request, draft and relay consumers keep their distinct public roles; renderer, catalog and platform gate converge on one exact alias owner. The door tool labels canonical function calls as write by name heuristic; this normalization is pure.

generality_proof: Explicit exact-name canonicalization applies before both runtime identity matching and platform classification, without a profile exemption or fuzzy prefix rule. Unknown alias-like future versions and three unrelated products remain rejected.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Canonicalize only curated exact legacy names while retaining unknown identity and namespace distinctions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Catalog and renderer parity regression covers legacy key, alias, models/ prefix and vendor namespace.
Same parity regression verifies shared normalization without changing explicit custom profiles.
Subprocess fixture tests accept existing aliases but reject unrelated and future alias-like products.

recurrence.reason: Future aliases can repeat the split between runtime-supported identity and spelling-based classification.

prevention.invariant: Exact same-product alias relationships have one canonical owner used by all repaired identity consumers.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown names retain their spelling; the existing platform-product classifier still rejects unrecognized multi-product combinations.
prevention.strategy: Add the existing aliases as exact identity data, consume it in both runtime resolvers and the classifier, retain the baseline and every existing legacy pattern.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove spelling-only identity inference for explicitly known aliases, not support for legacy identifiers.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Alias ownership is application data; no vendor request or dependency behavior changes.

migration: No saved data or generated pattern migration; old identifiers and Codex Img2 remain available.
residual_risks: Unregistered aliases still use existing spelling heuristics; the existing two-product blind spot is unchanged.
